title: YouTube SEO Checklist for 2026 (Technical + Content)
description: A practical checklist: titles, descriptions, chapters, chapters, playlists, and measurement—built for creators who want rankings without gimmicks.

sections.h2: Metadata that still moves the needle
sections.body: Titles and thumbnails drive CTR; the first lines of the description reinforce intent for Search. Use chapters when retention data shows confusion drops.
Treat playlists as topic pillars. Name them for clarity and link between related videos in the end screen and description.
CTR by impression source, average view duration by traffic source, and subscription rate from new viewers tell you where to iterate.

faq.question: Do tags still matter for YouTube SEO?
faq.answer: Tags are a minor signal compared to title, description, and viewer behavior. Use them for disambiguation, not stuffing.

faq.question: How often should I update old videos?
faq.answer: Prioritize high-impression, low-CTR assets first; update titles, thumbnails, and intros before touching long-tail winners.

title: What an AI YouTube Channel Audit Actually Does
description: How AI-assisted audits summarize patterns, surface gaps, and prioritize fixes—without replacing your creative judgment.

sections.body: Models excel at comparing many titles and topics to find weak CTR language and missing keyword angles.
Brand voice, storytelling, and community trust remain creator-led—AI should shorten analysis cycles, not replace taste.

faq.question: Will AI audits replace consultants?
faq.answer: They replace repetitive analysis, not strategy workshops or brand positioning.
